segments.he: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רָבָא: הָא דַּאֲמוּר רַבָּנַן זִיקַּת שְׁנֵי יְבָמִין, מִיחְלָץ חָלְצָה יַבּוֹמֵי לָא מִיַּבְּמָה, לָא תֵּימָא הֵיכָא דְּאִיכָּא צָרָה, דְּאִיכָּא לְמִגְזַר מִשּׁוּם צָרָה.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» If a brother performed levirate betrothal with a yevama and died, she has a levirate bond in relation to the remaining brothers from two deceased brothers. «Rava said:» With regard to «that which the Rabbis said,» that when «the bond of two yevamin» exists, «she performs ḥalitza and she does not enter into levirate marriage, you should not say» that «this» applies only «when there is a rival wife, as there is» reason «to decree due to a rival wife.» The suggestion is that as the rival wife can enter into levirate marriage by Torah law, if the woman who performed levirate betrothal with the second brother was also permitted to enter into levirate marriage, people might mistakenly permit levirate marriage to two rival wives from the same family.

segments.he: דְּהָא הָכָא לֵיכָּא צָרָה, מִיחְלָץ חָלְצָה, יַבּוֹמֵי לָא מִיַּבְּמָה.
segments.en: The proof that this is not the case is «that here,» in the first clause of the mishna, «there is no rival wife,» as it is referring to one woman, which means that this yevama who had relations with the nine-year-old is tied by the bonds of both her first husband and the underage yavam, whose intercourse is like levirate betrothal, and even so «she performs ḥalitza» but «she does not enter into levirate marriage.»
